source.title: Beyond Embedding Transfer: Component Roles in Grokking Transfer and Stability

record.tranche_reason: The study applies grokking-related transfer to cross-operator algorithmic tasks and reports acquisition and post-trigger stability results, an extension beyond the original single-task grokking setting.
record.gate_note: The study tests component transfer and stability during algorithmic-task transfer. It does not measure the claim's chance-to-near-perfect transition after training accuracy saturation, compare delay across training-set sizes, test gradual Fourier-circuit formation, use non-algorithmic or realistic large-model training, establish a critical dataset size or same-algorithm convergence, or test numerical-precision explanations for the original delay. Its results on acquisition and relapse are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study takes grokking on modular arithmetic and S5 as its setting. It reports only how its own warm-start transfer and post-trigger consolidation policies perform: acquisition speed versus cold start or E+U, and drawdown after the validation trigger. It never measures delayed generalization after training accuracy saturates, never varies training-set size against delay, and does not test the mechanism, regime, efficiency, algorithm-identity or artifact versions. The record's 'tests/T3' is downgraded to T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one refinement. The authors conclude that internal-block transfer accelerates acquisition beyond E+U in 1- and 2-layer models. Carriers (E+U) govern retention in 1-layer models. In 2-layer models, embeddings are required for acquisition via the B0↔B1 interface. A bounded post-trigger AdamW step budget (SH≈0.02, preserved second moments) suppresses drawdown to 0.02–0.20% across the tested modular and S5 tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Cross-operator warm-start transfer, component ablations, and post-trigger shielding/consolidation on modular arithmetic and S5; not a direct reproduction of from-scratch grokking. The cited original setup uses single-task training to study delayed generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with transferred components, model depth, target task, carrier freezing, post-trigger learning-rate schedule, and whether optimizer moments are preserved.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3: all 3 from-scratch runs that broke through (of 4) suffered relapses of 18.37, 13.86 and 29.95 pp after validation breakthrough under continued AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokked solutions on modular arithmetic can relapse transiently under continued AdamW training after breakthrough.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-trigger moment reset leaves ~23–24% drawdown. Removing weight decay worsens drawdown to 45–50%. A bounded step budget with preserved second moments cuts drawdown to ≤0.20%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-grokking stability depends on the post-trigger optimizer step budget and on weight decay.

record.problems: Evidence concerns transfer and post-trigger continuation rather than the original from-scratch grokking claim. Several conditions use small seed counts (commonly N = 12; some S5 results have 8/12 triggers), and some reported diagnostics are exploratory or test-conditioned. The paper does not test how grokking delay changes with training-set size.
record.rows_left_out: Additional post-trigger ablations and schedules, including moment reset, weight-decay removal, low learning rate, cosine schedules, and further pinning variants, are reported in Tables 6–8 but omitted to keep the record focused on the principal acquisition and stability outcomes. Additional probe/state-swap diagnostics in §4 and Appendix A are not rows for any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No training-accuracy saturation timing and no train-fraction sweep of delay. Cold-start runs only show late validation breakthrough (~21–27k steps) at a fixed 20% split.
No Fourier-circuit or progress-measure analysis of the generalizing transition. Probes and state-swaps concern post-grokking relapse.
Only algorithmic tasks. Frobenius rescaling controls transfer scale but does not test lazy-to-rich or norm switching of the delay.
Weight decay is fixed at λ=1.0 during acquisition. There is no critical dataset size or ungrokking test; post-trigger weight-decay removal concerns relapse only.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
AdamW step-size effects are studied only for post-trigger relapse, not as a cause of the original delay. Floating-point precision is not varied as a cause.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-author preprint on grokking transfer and post-grokking relapse. Every row compares the study's own transfer or consolidation conditions, so all rows carry versions ['none']. No verdicts are given because no claim version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test delayed generalization after training accuracy saturation or whether delay grows as the training set shrinks.
Does not measure gradual formation of a generalizing Fourier circuit or progress measures anticipating a generalization jump.
Tests algorithmic tasks, not non-algorithmic data or a lazy-to-rich transition induced by initialization scale or weight norm.
Does not study LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Does not test whether low norm favors an efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
Does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
Studies optimizer interventions on post-trigger relapse, not whether optimizer or numerical choices produce the original grokking delay.
